problem_type: Credential-bearing vendor and onboarding requests followed redirects without constraining the next origin
symptom: A local two-port HTTP fixture showed a 302/307/308 response forwarding custom authentication headers to the second port; 307/308 also replayed the POST body.
direct_cause: vendorHttp delegated to vendorBaseFallback and onboardingIpc delegated to appFetch without a redirect option, so native fetch used its default follow behavior. The outbound guard checked only the initial URL.
class_root: Credential-bearing requests lacked a transport invariant that rejects redirects before a later hop can receive headers, query credentials, or a request body.
affected_population: Any vendor generation or binary request carrying an API key, tenant key, authorization header, custom gateway header, or POST body
Users testing a custom onboarding endpoint whose first response is a cross-origin redirect
Any 302, 307, or 308 response produced by a provider, relay, proxy, captive portal, or misconfigured endpoint
entry_points: electron/vendor/vendorBaseFallback.ts fetchVendorWithBaseFallback first and fallback sends
internal_only_reason: The invariant is an application transport rule enforced at Nomi's request boundaries; the audited behavior is determined by the native fetch contract and this repository's credential ownership, not by a provider API specification.

invariant_owner_layer.rationale: The vendor wrapper owns the shared credentialed vendor transport and the onboarding protocol probe is the second audited credentialed boundary. Both now fail closed before a redirect hop; their local two-port tests exercise the class invariant rather than mocking fetch behavior.

invariants: Credential-bearing vendor requests never auto-follow a redirect
Credential-bearing onboarding protocol probes never auto-follow a redirect
A redirect response cannot cause a second-origin request containing authorization, x-api-key, x-tenant-key, other custom auth headers, or a sensitive POST body
The existing no-redirect model-list pagination contract remains manual and rejects unsafe cross-origin pagination links

door_reduction.why_not: The two audited request families cannot be merged without changing their contracts: vendorHttp must preserve vendor base fallback/retry semantics, while onboarding probeOneProtocol must preserve protocol-specific POST bodies and optional per-connection dispatchers. The vendor call has a caller door plus the shared fallback wrapper, and onboarding registration remains a separate main-process installation door. The fix puts the same fail-closed redirect invariant at both shared request boundaries instead of adding a third global classifier.

generality_proof: The repository scan and door map found the confirmed vendor request caller, its fallback wrapper, the onboarding protocol probe, and the existing manual model-list transport. The vendor wrapper applies redirect:error to both the first and official fallback sends, so every requestVendor JSON or binary operation receives the invariant. probeOneProtocol applies it to every onboarding protocol candidate. fetchModelList already uses redirect:manual and validates every pagination link's origin/path, so it remains fail-closed. Other raw appFetch callers (including AI SDK, multipart, and audio paths) are recorded as residual follow-up work rather than being falsely declared fixed by this focused remediation.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Owns both first-send and official fallback vendor transport options and rejects redirects for each credential-bearing request.
Owns protocol-test POST construction and now fails closed before credentials or probe body can be replayed through a redirect.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The requestVendor call reaches fetchVendorWithBaseFallback for JSON and binary vendor operations; the wrapper now sets redirect:error for both sends.
All onboarding test-connection protocol candidates converge on this function, which now sets redirect:error on the credential-bearing POST.
This separately audited onboarding listing path already sends redirect:manual and rejects unsafe cross-origin pagination links; its focused test asserts no second request follows a redirect.

The fallback ladder probe is an unauthenticated GET used only to identify an official candidate. It does not carry user credentials or a sensitive body; credentialed sends use the fetchVendorWithBaseFallback boundary above.

This is a separate raw appFetch/AI SDK transport surface and is explicitly retained as follow-up residual risk; the current audit finding and regression scope are vendorHttp fallback plus onboarding protocol probing.

recurrence.reason: Redirect handling is transport behavior. Any provider, relay, captive portal, proxy, or future caller can return a redirect, and custom headers/body replay is independent of provider identity.

prevention.invariant: Every vendor request sent through the fallback wrapper receives redirect:error on both its initial and official fallback send.
prevention.failure_mode: Native fetch rejects the redirect before a second-origin request is made; the caller reports a network failure and does not retry through an unvalidated hop.
prevention.strategy: Set the policy at the earliest shared credential-bearing transport boundaries. Keep model-list pagination's existing manual-and-revalidate contract and do not add a parallel global classifier.

legacy_paths.rationale: No legacy redirect helper is retained or removed; the existing fetch entry points remain and now receive an explicit fail-closed option.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency upgrade is needed. The fix binds the application invariant through RequestInit and existing native fetch behavior.

migration: No persisted data or external contract changes. Existing same-origin success responses and official fallback retry behavior remain unchanged; redirect responses now fail visibly before a second request.
residual_risks: Raw appFetch callers outside the confirmed vendor/onboarding paths, including AI SDK, multipart, audio, and native endpoint probes, need a separate audit and policy owner; this PR does not claim those paths are fixed.
Live providers, paid requests, domestic no-proxy networking, and Electron/Playwright GUI execution remain untested in the current environment.
